title: The flight into Egypt (Matthew 2:13–23)
hookLine: the holy family become refugees, fleeing a king's violence by night

cards: A family packs in the dark. No time for goodbyes. Whatever fits in their arms, and a child who doesn't understand why he's been woken.

They leave before sunrise, heading for a border, because staying means someone they love may be killed. That happens somewhere in the world tonight. In Matthew's Gospel it happens to Mary, Joseph and the child.
The magi have gone home another way, and Herod, the king who asked where the child was, has worked out that he's been tricked. And Joseph has another dream.

teach.b: The angel's words are urgent: "Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him."
Joseph does it that same night. He never speaks a single word in the Gospels. He just gets up and goes.
Then comes the darkest scene in the Christmas story. Herod, furious, orders every boy of two and under in and around Bethlehem to be killed.
Matthew is the only source for this; no other writer of the time mentions it, though Herod was known to be ruthless, even with his own sons.
Matthew quotes the prophet Jeremiah: "Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not." The story doesn't hurry past the grief.
Churches still keep a day for these children, the Holy Innocents, in the days after Christmas. And Egypt, the old land of slavery in the Exodus story, is now the place of safety.

teach.h: OUT OF EGYPT HAVE I CALLED MY SON.
teach.b: Matthew quotes another prophet, Hosea: "Out of Egypt have I called my son." Israel's story, lived again in one child.
Coptic Christians in Egypt still trace the places they say the family stayed, and celebrate its arrival every year.
Then Herod dies, Joseph dreams again, and they come home, not to Bethlehem but to a small town in Galilee called Nazareth.

teach.h: A CHILD CARRIED ACROSS A BORDER BY NIGHT.
teach.b: Before he preached, before he healed, before anyone knew his name, Jesus was a child carried across a border by night.

how: Many churches remember the flight into Egypt in the days after Christmas, along with the Holy Innocents, and many Christian charities point to this story in their work with refugees. Coptic Christians celebrate the Holy Family's arrival in Egypt each year and visit places tradition links to their journey.

practice: Think of one family that has had to leave home, someone you know, someone you saw in the news, or your own family a generation or two back, and picture them clearly: the packing, the road, the first night somewhere strange.
If you pray, pray for them by name, or for the family whose name you'll never know; if you don't, just keep them in mind with care.

wordCard.voice: Holy Innocents. The name churches still use for the children Herod had killed in and around Bethlehem, grieved in Matthew's Gospel and remembered every year after Christmas.

orig.note: Greek: flee! The angel's command to Joseph, a cousin of the Latin fugere that gave English fugitive.

carryVoice: Your line: he was a refugee first. Before the sermons, the road. Day forty-five, done.
